summary: Wallowa-Whitman NF pole lookout on Wood Butte: a 40-foot L-4 tower dated 1935, staffed into the 1960s, removed or destroyed in 1966.

facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1966; no source read describes what remains at the site.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Wallowa-Whitman National Forest

events.note: Per diem lookout J.W. Wood used a high point near his home; before he died he asked that half an acre be deeded to the Forest Service
Oregon Lookouts page: a new lookout tower was constructed (conflicts with the 1935 register date)
Forest note calls the lookout not satisfactory and says it should be abandoned, with a lookout placed in section 30
Steven Crow listed as lookout; last staffing entry on firelookout.com
Manned only after lightning storms and during extreme fire weather
Vandals broke two windows in August while the tower was unoccupied
Register says removed; firelookout.com says destroyed

evidence.supports: Lookout tower located on the Powwatka Ridge road
evidence.quote: the Wood Butte Lookout tower, located on the Powwatka Ridge road, was broken into during the latter part of August

evidence.supports: J.W. Wood used a high point near his home; half an acre deeded request, 1927
evidence.quote: He used a high point near his home for a lookout point, and before he died he requested that one-half acre on this point be deeded to the Forest Service.
A new lookout tower was constructed.

evidence.supports: Construction of the tower took 699 man-hours (dated 1936 on the page)
evidence.quote: Construction of this tower required 699 man hours of labor
Built in 1935, this 40' pole L-4 tower was removed in 1966.
Known lookout personnel: 1936: Ray Knudson; 1941: Harold Lamb

evidence.supports: Marvin Wiggans 1942-1943; other staff listed through 1963
evidence.quote: 1942-1943: Marvin Wiggans; 1946: Bill Dailey; 1954: Ed Carper; 1955: Bill Colpitts; 1956-1957: Glenn Grimes; 1961: Bob Bennett; 1962: Kenneth Ostrander, Wendell Weaver; 1963: Steven Crow.

evidence.supports: 1953 forest note: not satisfactory, should be abandoned, lookout in section 30
evidence.quote: Woods Butte Lookout is not satisfactory, should be abandoned and a lookout located in section 30, T5N, R44E.

evidence.supports: Manned only after lightning storms and in extreme fire weather, 1966
evidence.quote: The lookout is manned only after lightning storms and during periods of extreme fire weather.

evidence.supports: Two windows broken by vandals, August 1966
evidence.quote: Vandals entered the lookout tower by breaking two of the windows.

evidence.supports: Tower unoccupied at the time of the vandalism
evidence.quote: The tower was unoccupied at the time.

evidence.supports: Wallowa County Chieftain report on the August vandalism: sheriff investigated, no definite evidence found
evidence.quote: Sheriff Mark Marks investigated the vandalism, however, no definite evidence was found.

evidence.supports: Register's latest picture is a 2009 photo of the site
evidence.quote: Wood Butte Lookout site 2009 - courtesy of Ron Kemnow

corrections.why: Both the register and firelookout.com give a 40-foot pole tower (about 12.2 m). The record's 15.2 m is not in either source.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give 1935 for the 40-foot tower. The Oregon Lookouts page gives a new tower in 1932 and labor for 'this tower' in 1936. The story uses 1935 and reports the other dates as a disagreement.

sources.title: Wood Butte Lookout Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites Register, Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: Built date conflict: 1935 (register, firelookout.com) versus 1932 and 1936 labor entry (Oregon Lookouts page, which quotes Six Twenty-Six). Removal conflict: removed (register, Oregon Lookouts 'Removed') versus destroyed (firelookout.com), both 1966. The 1957 accident item on the Oregon Lookouts page was left out. The Oregon Lookouts page also carries a 1946 Coast and Geodetic Survey station description for the summit (PID RA1137); it does not describe present conditions. No source read describes the site today, and none states whether the point is open to visitors, so no access level is set.
